sources.text:
Hyderabad is rationing piped water to once every three days and fining pubs up to Rs 20,000 for washing floors with drinking water. But videos of water gushing onto streets in two localities have left residents asking who will answer for those leaks.  
  
In one video, from Maula Ali, Manjeera water is seen running down a road. In the other, from SR Nagar, water spills from a pump outside JJ Hospital.  
  
Both clips spread on social media, with users asking who was responsible for letting water go to waste in the middle of a crisis.  
  
“Restaurants and pubs were asked to pay a Rs 20,000 fine for wasting water. Who should be penalised for this pump, which is leaking water?” asked Mohammed Ilyas, who posted the SR Nagar video on Instagram.  
  
Fines for some:  
The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) has been fining people, restaurants and pubs between Rs 5,000 and Rs 20,000 for wasting water while cleaning their premises. One city pub was recently fined Rs 20,000.  
  
From November 1, water tankers caught spilling drinking water on the way will also be fined Rs 5,000. HMWSSB Managing Director K Ashok Reddy issued the order on October 24 after the board found tankers being overfilled and water splashing onto roads.  
  
Tankers with leaks, missing lids or loose covers will not be filled until they are repaired.  
  
The Maula Ali leak has struck a nerve because the Manjeera is one of the sources under the most strain. The board expects a shortfall of about 100 million gallons a day (MGD) from Singur and Manjeera between January and August.

# HMWSSB warns residents against water wastage, threatens to disconnect services

Published - September 21, 2026 07:45 pm IST - HYDERABAD

The Hindu Bureau

SEE ALL
Remove

The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply & Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) has issued serious warning against water wastage, after imposing penalties in five such instances on Monday. Second time offenders will attract disconnection of water supply, it warned.

All the five penalised were residents of Jubilee Hills, and found to have been wasting water, during inspections conducted by the Board officials.

The inspections will be intensified in the coming days, and second time offenders will be penalised through disconnection of water supply, the note warned.

Using drinking water to wash floor and vehicles, leaving the tap open, and not shutting down the pump set even after overhead tank overflows are some of the instances of water wastage, as shared by the Board.

Despite awareness campaigns and warnings, the users are still found resorting to the same practices, calling for penalties. The penalties which had started with just ₹1000 per instance, have over the time risen to ₹5,000, then ₹10,000 and now ₹20,000. Still the violations continue to persist. the note said.

Leakages in the water supply network too will be plugged by officials within 24 hours of identification, and in case of dereliction of duties, action will be taken against officials and staff too. The water board’s drinking water pipeline extends to 15,000 kilometres in the city, to plug leakages in which, a special action plan is being be taken up. The officials have been directed to identify locations with frequent leakages and provide permanent solutions.
